key_insight: MoSE3 moves beyond tracking 2D pixels or 3D points and predicts full 6-DoF rigid motion at every pixel in a scene. This gives a denser, more physically meaningful view of motion by capturing both translation and rotation in world space.
problem_solved: Traditional dense tracking methods mostly estimate where pixels move, but not how objects rotate or which pixels belong to the same moving rigid body. The paper addresses the need for per-pixel SE(3) motion from monocular RGB video.
method: Uses a feed-forward model to predict dense world-space SE(3) transforms directly from monocular RGB video.
Outputs a rigid motion estimate for every pixel, rather than only sparse tracks or translation vectors.
Provides a representation that groups pixels by shared rigid motion while preserving full 6-DoF motion information.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this enables richer motion understanding in dynamic scenes, which can improve tasks like tracking, segmentation, scene reconstruction, and robot perception. It also offers a more physically grounded representation than translation-only point tracking.

paper_title: MoSE3: Learning World-Space SE(3) at Every Pixel
paper_authors: Jiahuan Cheng, Zhiyi Li, Tian Xia, Ruojin Cai, Yilun Du
